title: Pan-Seared Pork Loin, Mustard Sauce
summary: Seared pork loin medallions finished in a quick creamy Dijon-mustard pan sauce.

assumptions.note: Source recipe reads as 4 servings (700 g pork); amounts below are x1.5. Scale back down if 4 is actually correct.
Rimi's plain 'vegetable oil' shelf item is rapeseed (rapšu eļļa). Swap for sunflower oil if you prefer.
Recipe names both as the preferred option ('Dijon or regular', 'smoked paprika works great'). Use plain mustard/sweet paprika if you'd rather.

assumptions.text: Frying pan is generic, not tracked
assumptions.note: No specific frying pan is logged in the kitchen inventory; use any large frying pan/skillet that fits pork in a single uncrowded layer.

assumptions.text: Only the pork dish is planned in detail
assumptions.note: Salad, mash, rice, and bread are serving suggestions from the source recipe, not planned here — ask if you want one of them worked out too.

assumptions.text: AEG hob heat settings, model unconfirmed
assumptions.note: Owned hob is AEG/Electrolux, 4 zones, heat 0-9 + Booster; exact model logged as representative (IBX64200CB). Adjust settings to your hob's actual response.

steps.title: Weigh and slice pork
steps.do: Weigh the pork loin on the kitchen scale, then slice it across the grain into pieces about 1-1.5 cm thick. Cutting across the grain, not with it, keeps each piece tender.

steps.title: Season pork
steps.do: Rub the sliced pork on both sides with salt, ground black pepper, and smoked paprika. Coat evenly so every piece browns and tastes the same.
steps.done: Spices visible and even on every slice

steps.title: Slice onion, mince garlic
steps.do: Slice the onions thinly and mince the garlic; keep them separate since the garlic goes in later. Fine mincing on the garlic stops it burning once it hits the hot pan.
steps.done: Onion in thin half-moons, garlic finely minced

steps.title: Sear pork in batches
steps.do: Heat the oil in the frying pan over high heat and sear the pork in 2-3 uncrowded batches, about 1-1.5 minutes per side until well browned. Crowding the pan steams the meat instead of browning it. Set seared pork aside.
steps.done: Pork deeply browned, not yet cooked through

steps.title: Cook onion and garlic
steps.do: In the same pan, lower the heat and cook the onion 3-4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds more. Same pan keeps the browned pork bits for flavour; the garlic only needs seconds before it turns bitter.
steps.done: Onion translucent, garlic fragrant not browned

steps.title: Build mustard sauce
steps.do: Pour in the cream and stir in the mustard and thyme, simmering gently until combined. A light simmer stops the cream from splitting.
steps.done: Sauce lightly thickened, mustard fully blended

steps.title: Simmer pork in sauce
steps.do: Return the seared pork and its resting juices to the pan and simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, just until cooked through. Pork loin is lean, so pull it the moment it's no longer pink at the centre to keep it juicy.
steps.done: Pork no longer pink at centre, sauce coats a spoon

steps.title: Taste, adjust, and serve
steps.do: Taste the sauce and adjust salt and pepper as needed, then serve hot with your chosen sides. Salad, mash, rice, or crusty bread all pair well.

food_safety: Wash hands and boards after handling raw pork
Pork must reach no visible pink at the centre before serving
